occupancy.rationale: Share of licensed beds that are occupied and billed. No occupancy or vacancy data for NJ licensed community residences was found (see not_claimed), so 92% default (88% conservative, 96% optimistic) is an operator estimate, not a sourced statistic. Demand context: 3,665 people on the CCP Priority Waiting List in FY26, with DDD reaching roughly 200-400 a year from it [S43][S44]. A listed person is not guaranteed enrollment [S45], and a new provider does not receive a guaranteed referral pipeline.

configurations.label: One 4-bed group home (assumed $150,000 per resident per year authorized)
configurations.notes: Smallest realistic licensed-home start. Revenue is an ASSUMPTION: DDD's 2026 residential Individual Supports rates were not found (see not_claimed). The only sourced residential-level figures are the CCP Individual Supports annual allotments, from $66,424 (Tier A) to $527,838 (Tier Ea), per a secondary guide [S27]. $150,000/resident/year ($12,500/month) is an operator assumption inside that range, not a published rate. Replace it with the actual authorized amounts. The state requires 24 months of prior direct care service history before a licensing application [S7], so this model assumes the applicant already has that history. Resident room-and-board contributions are not modeled because the rules were not verified, which understates revenue.

N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.8 requires a two-week schedule with an in-charge employee per shift [S2], but no awake-overnight or per-shift ratio was found in 10:44A (see not_claimed); the awake/asleep ratio found is in 10:44C and does not apply. Wage = DDD's projected NJ average DSP wage after the 1/1/2026 rate increase, $20.71/hr [S24]. NJ minimum wage is $15.92 [S30]. A $18.92/hr long-term-care direct care rate appears in a secondary source [S33]; applicability to DD residences is unconfirmed, and $20.71 is above it. O*NET/BLS NJ home health aide median is $37,090/year, about $17.83/hr [S37].

staffing.role: Executive director / agency head (licensee or hired)
staffing.notes: 0.5 FTE x $95,000 operator estimate, no BLS wage verified. An owner-operator lacking any one must hire a qualifying executive director, which changes this salary line. Whether a waiver or variance is available was not checked. sections.executive_summary:
New Jersey licenses small residential settings for adults with developmental disabilities (DD) under **N.J.A.C. 10:44A**, administered by the NJ DHS **Office of Licensing**. The covered models are group homes, supervised apartments and supportive living [S6]. A license is needed when the setting is provider-managed [S1]. A community residence may house up to 16 individuals, and a supervised apartment up to four per apartment [S2][S3]. Operating without Office of Licensing authorization is prohibited [S4]. A different chapter, N.J.A.C. 10:44B, covers private-home models such as Family Care and Skill Development [S2]. The chapter was readopted effective February 17, 2026 and now expires February 17, 2033. DHS said further rulemaking may be needed, and no pending amendment was found [S6].

**The entry barrier is experience, not a license fee.** Before applying, an agency must document at least 24 months of prior direct care service history, including survey or audit results and plans of correction [S7]. The application starts with DDD's Combined Application to Become a Medicaid/DDD Approved Provider, selecting *Individual Supports* [S4][S7]. It must include an independent CPA examination of the organization's finances for the two most recent fiscal years, professional references and corporate documents [S4]. After a completed application, DHS has 60 calendar days to approve or not approve it [S4]. A first-time operator with no service history cannot apply directly. Confirm with the DDD Provider Helpdesk how the 24 months can be shown.

**Money flows fee-for-service from Medicaid through DDD.** The adult waivers are the Supports Program and the Community Care Program (CCP), authorized under the NJ FamilyCare Section 1115 demonstration. CCP is the waiver with a waiting list [S9][S10][S11][S45]. Providers bill after delivering services [S12]. **The 2026 DDD residential Individual Supports rates, procedure codes and billing units could not be found in any retrieved source.** Every revenue figure in the financial model is therefore an assumption, not a published rate. It is set within the CCP Individual Supports annual allotment range of $66,424 to $527,838 reported by a secondary guide [S27]. Replace it with your authorized amounts before relying on any result.

**Demand is large but slot-limited.** DDD reported 3,665 people on the CCP Priority Waiting List in FY26 (+511 from FY25), and 28,783 individuals served in total [S43]. DDD typically reaches 200 to 400 people a year from that list [S44]. A new provider has no guaranteed referral pipeline.

**Profitability is thin and depends on scale and on the unverified rate.** At the default 92% occupancy and the assumed $150,000 per resident per year, three 4-bed homes (the default) earn about **$1,765 a month (1.3% margin)**, with break-even occupancy of 90.8%. Six 4-bed homes earn about $11,432 a month (4.1%). A single 6-bed home earns about $8,694 a month (12.6%), but it leans on the same unverified rate and staffing assumptions. A single 4-bed home loses about $1,933 a month, and two lower-tier supervised apartments lose about $9,385 a month.
sections.service_model:
**Who is served.** DDD adult services are for people age 21 and older [S10]. The CCP waiting list accepts people 18 and older who are eligible for or enrolled in Medicaid and meet DDD functional criteria [S45]. Waiver enrollment requires age 21+ and Medicaid eligibility [S10].

**What a licensed community residence is.** Chapter 10:44A applies to provider-managed program models, including group homes and supervised apartments [S2]. The readoption notice also lists supportive living [S6]. OPIA says licensure is required when the setting is provider-managed, when a CCP-enrolled individual lives there, or when the individual service plan (ISP) documents a need for personal guidance [S1]. In this research, a "community residence" under the chapter means a home housing up to 16 individuals with developmental disabilities [S2]. Supervised apartments hold up to four individuals per apartment [S3]. A residence may not be located on the grounds of, or immediately adjacent to, public institutions serving a similar population [S2].

**Models outside this bundle.** Community care residences (a private home or apartment under Family Care or Skill Development) are licensed under N.J.A.C. 10:44B, not 10:44A [S2][S3]. This report covers only the provider-managed 10:44A models.

**Program structure.** DDD runs two Medicaid waiver programs, the Supports Program and the Community Care Program [S9]. Both sit under New Jersey's Section 1115 demonstration [S10]. The former Community Care Waiver stopped operating under 1915(c) authority, and the CCW moved to the 1115 Comprehensive Medicaid Waiver in November 2017 [S11]. In the model, the residential service is called *Individual Supports* because that is the service an agency must select on the combined application to run a licensed residential setting [S7].

**Regulatory framework to expect.** The Office of Licensing inspects annually, may inspect without notice, and says it is increasing unannounced inspections beginning in 2026 [S1][S4]. DHS also has expanded enforcement authority over DD providers under P.L.2025, c.280, enacted January 2026 [S43]. The content of that law was not retrieved.
sections.licensing_pathway:
**Step 0: Confirm you qualify to apply.** DDD requires at least 24 months of documented prior direct care service history, including survey or audit results and plans of correction, before the licensing application [S7]. No license is issued to a person previously denied a license by any State agency for substantial noncompliance [S4].

**Step 1: Form the entity and get housing guidance.** OPIA advises: do not acquire housing before consulting DDD's Office of Housing and Resource Development [S1]. Siting limits apply [S2]. Municipal zoning and Uniform Construction Code fire-safety specifics were not researched or verified.

**Step 2: Submit the Combined Application.** Licensure is initiated by completing and mailing the Combined Application to Become a Medicaid/DDD Approved Provider, with the Attestation for Individual Supports Provider [S4]. On DDD's page, agencies that want to run a licensed residence must select Individual Supports [S7]. The application includes:

- an independent CPA examination of the organization's financial status for the two most recent fiscal years, with Management Letters [S4];
- at least three professional references each for the applicant and the executive director [S4];
- proof of authorization to do business in New Jersey and organizational and governance documents [S4].

The agency head cannot be paid or contracted until a criminal history record check clears. If the agency head is not the owner or licensee, the owner or licensee must also complete a check [S4]. The executive director qualifications in N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.5(a) are cumulative. The licensee or executive director must have (1) a bachelor's degree, (2) five years of progressive management experience working with people with DD, at least two of them supervisory at a senior or administrative level, and (3) knowledge of program design, staff development and fiscal standards. The application must demonstrate compliance (10:44A-1.4(c)(1)(iv)) [S2]. An owner lacking any one must hire a qualifying executive director. Whether a waiver or variance is available was not checked.

**Step 3: Meet the application clock.** If all required elements are not received within **45 days** of the initial submission, the application may be denied, and the applicant is barred from reapplying for six months [S4]. DHS must give written approval or non-approval within **60 calendar days** of receiving the completed application. It can extend that period only in exceptional circumstances [S4].

**Step 4: Pre-opening submissions.** The applicant submits a procedure manual to the Office of Licensing for approval. It then submits job descriptions for each table-of-organization position to DDD for review and approval [S4].

**Step 5: Medicaid and DDD enrollment.** An agency must be a Medicaid-approved provider before it can submit claims for DDD services [S13]. The same Combined Application is used to become both a Medicaid and a DDD approved provider [S13]. Since January 1, 2023, NJ Medicaid claims deny for providers not registered with Medicaid or without a Medicaid ID [S14]. The CY2026 federal enrollment application fee is $750 per a consultant source that limits it to institutional providers. It is per service location and not annual, and whether it applies to DDD residential providers was not verified [S15].

**Step 6: License term and inspections.** A full license is effective for up to one year [S2]. Every residence is subject to an annual on-site inspection and to DHS inspection without limitation or notice [S4]. Inspections review staff files, schedules, credentials and background checks [S1]. Partial compliance can produce a provisional license, and two consecutive provisional licenses may result in non-renewal [S1]. Administrative reviews also look at insurance documents [S1].

**What could not be verified.** No Office of Licensing application, license, renewal or inspection fee was found in the 10:44A-1.4 text reviewed, so none is claimed. The timeline from a complete application to first admission beyond the 60-day decision window, renewal timelines, and the current Office of Licensing phone and mailing address were not verified. Whether the 2022 proposal for a combined license application (PRN 2022-083) was adopted was not verified, although the rule text on Cornell LII refers to the combined application [S4]. The text reviewed is the 2023 chapter version. The 2026 readoption notice was reviewed, but the readopted text itself was not [S6].
sections.reimbursement:
**How money flows.** DDD has substantially shifted its service delivery system to fee-for-service [S11]. Providers bill Medicaid for specific services delivered to each individual after the service is provided, rather than receiving monthly contract allotments [S12]. An agency must be Medicaid-approved before it can submit claims [S13]. Plan for a billing lag and keep cash reserves for it.

**Two waivers, one real pipeline.** The Supports Program has no waiting list, but CCP does [S45]. The CCP Individual Supports allotment is much larger because it is for residential-level care. A secondary guide citing DDD's FY26 Quick Guide reports annual budgets of $28,635 (Tier A) to $113,205 (Tier Ea) for the Supports Program, and CCP Individual Supports allotments of **$66,424 (Tier A) to $527,838 (Tier Ea)**, effective January 1, 2026 [S27]. The DDD primary document was not retrieved. These allotments are budget caps, not rates and not payment guarantees.

**The rate gap.** DDD has published FY26 fee-for-service rates effective January 1, 2026, in a Quick Guide with procedure codes and FY25 and FY26 rate columns. Individual Supports uses H2016HI-series daily tier codes. The Individual Supports rows could not be read in the retrieved material, so the rate amounts, tier codes and billing units used for residential revenue are not verified, and every revenue figure in the model is an assumption. The only DDD schedule retrieved in full is a May 2015 cost-study schedule. It lists Support Coordination at $239.81 per member per month. That figure is stale, superseded by the 7/2023 and 7/2024 rate changes, and not used [S22]. Its Community Based Supports line ($28.03, no confirmed unit) and old Individual Supports daily tier rates are also not used.

**Recent rate and budget movement (context, not a price).**

- Effective January 1, 2026, DDD raised rates for nine agency-provided services, as set out in its 12/30/2025 Information Bulletin and Quick Guide. The increase funds a DSP and DSP Supervisor wage increase of about $0.46 per hour, supported by a $9.1M state allocation. Agencies must pass it through as a base-wage increase (not a bonus or operating expense) no later than March 1, 2026, including retroactive pay. It is not margin.
- A separate nine-service rate increase tied to new DSP training requirements took effect October 1, 2024 [S23].
- DDD projects the average NJ DSP wage at about $20.71 per hour ($20.25 NCI 2024 average plus about $0.46); DDD also cites about $21 per hour for 2026 [S24].
- A July 2022 FY23 appropriation raised Individual Supports (Residential) rates by about 1% overall ($7.5M state funds) [S28]. This is historical only.
- The FY26 State Budget added about $164 million to DDD's budget [S25]. DDD community programs' gross funding was $3.81 billion in FY26, per the Governor's recommendation [S46]. The FY27 recommendation is $4.12 billion, including an additional $154.0 million in State funds for CCP and the Supports Program [S47][S48]. Whether the FY27 budget, DSP and supervisor rate increases, and the proposed removal of 318 people from the CCP waiting list were enacted was not verified [S26][S43].

**Room and board and resident income.** How room and board or a client contribution works in DDD residences was not found in any retrieved DDD or SSA source. The 2026 SSI federal benefit rate for an individual is $994 per month (secondary source; the SSA primary page was not fetched) [S17]. The financial model therefore includes no room-and-board revenue, which understates revenue.

**Other billing requirements.**

- **EVV:** DDD Individual Supports and In-Home Respite codes are on NJ's EVV list (for example H2016HI, H2016HI22 and H2016HIU88 for Individual Supports). Community Based Supports at 15 minutes (H2021HI22) are also covered [S18][S19]. NJ's contracted vendor is HHAeXchange [S20]. EVV went live January 1, 2021 [S21]. CMS allows exclusion when the caregiver lives with the person receiving care, with a Live-In Worker Attestation [S19]. Whether and how EVV applies to a given group home billing pattern should be confirmed with DDD.
- **Audit and fiscal reporting:** Agencies claiming $350,000 or more in combined CCP and Supports Program reimbursement must meet an annual financial statement audit requirement, performed under GAAS [S8]. Agencies with more than $350,000 in annual DDD billing must also file an annual Fiscal Sustainability Report on DDD's template, due 120 calendar days after the state fiscal year ends (about October 30), emailed to DDD.WaiverFinancialReports@dhs.nj.gov [S8].
- **Managed care:** DDD sources describe fee-for-service, but no managed-care carve-out text was retrieved.

**Private pay is not the model.** DD residences are funded through DDD. For benchmarking only, CareScout's 2025 survey puts the NJ median assisted living community at $101,550 per year (about $8,462 per month) [S29]. That measures private-pay assisted living, not DD residential services.
sections.demand:
**Waiting list and served population.** DDD's June 2026 update reports the CCP Priority Waiting List at **3,665 people in FY26, up 511 from FY25**. FY18 was 2,592. Total individuals served by DDD were 28,783 in FY26, up 1,586 [S43]. DDD attributes the rise to an influx of individuals entering DDD services and more applications. It says many people were added retroactively, so ranks moved little [S43]. The 2026 ranking letters were mailed on June 24, 2026 [S43]. A March 2026 advocacy report of a DHS briefing said more than 30,000 adults are served [S26]. This differs from the DDD budget table figure, and this report uses the DDD figure.

**Throughput is limited by budget.** DDD says it typically reaches between 200 and 400 people a year from the Priority Waiting List (FY22: 200; FY23: 400) [S44]. The same 2024 presentation counted 4,394 people on the full CCP waiting list (2,580 priority and 1,814 general) [S44]. A current general-list figure was not found. The FY27 budget as proposed funds removal of 318 people from the priority list, but enactment was not verified [S43]. The administration said it is working toward addressing the CCP waitlist in the coming year [S26].

**What the list does and does not mean.** DDD works through the list chronologically and checks eligibility when a person is reached. Being listed does not guarantee eligibility or enrollment [S45]. For a provider, the list shows unmet need. It does not guarantee admissions, and a provider has no guaranteed referral pipeline. The referral-source breakdown (support coordination agencies, families, hospitals, schools) and any residential-specific waitlist count were not found.

**Supply context.** The Office of Licensing reports 2,300 licensed homes with a combined capacity to serve over 9,600 individuals [S16]. The page is undated, and whether the figure includes traumatic brain injury (TBI) residences was not verified. The licensed agency list is dated October 28, 2025 [S49]. Occupancy and vacancy rates for licensed residences were not found. The model's 92% occupancy is an operator estimate.
sections.operations:
**Staffing rules that were verified.**

- Direct support professionals must be at least 18 years old with a high school diploma or equivalent [S3].
- The residence supervisor needs a high school diploma or equivalent and one year of experience working with people with DD [S3].
- The licensee or executive director must meet cumulative requirements under N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.5(a): a bachelor's degree, five years of progressive management experience working with people with DD (at least two supervisory at a senior or administrative level), and knowledge of program design, staff development and fiscal standards [S2]. An owner lacking any one must hire a qualifying executive director.
- Each residence must keep a written staff schedule covering at least two weeks, with the in-charge employee designated for each shift [S2].
- Staff need not be on site when no individuals are present, but trained staff familiar with residents must be available for emergencies [S2].
- Each specialized training must be completed by at least one person on every shift (10:44A-2.8(b)). Build this into the schedule.

**What was not found.** No awake-overnight or per-shift staffing ratio for 10:44A residences was found. The awake/asleep ratio located is in 10:44C (head injury) and does not apply. No initial or annual training hour totals were found. Staffing in the model is therefore an operator estimate sized to resident need, not a rule-derived number. Verify against the current rule text and each resident's ISP.

**Wage pass-through (mandatory).** DDD requires agencies to pass the FY26 rate increase through to DSPs and DSP Supervisors as a base-wage increase of about $0.46 per hour, effective January 1, 2026, no later than March 1, 2026, including retroactive pay. It cannot be paid as a bonus or used for operating expenses. Make sure DSP and supervisor wages reflect it, and do not count it as margin.

**Training.** Within 90 days of employment each DSP must complete DDD Shifting Expectations, preventing abuse and neglect, and ECC first aid and CPR, each with a valid certificate on file [S5]. Medication training and demonstrated competency are required before staff give any medication, and the competency check is annual. Specialized training (feeding, mobility, seizures, mental health, behavior support plans) is required within 90 days (10:44A-2.7, 2.8).

**Background checks and screening.** The agency head, and the owner or licensee when different, must clear a criminal history check [S4]. DDD-approved providers must also run staff criminal history checks before hire, Central Registry of Offenders and Child Abuse Registry checks, pre-employment and random controlled-substance testing, and driver abstract checks for staff who transport. Inspectors review staff files, schedules, credentials and background checks [S1]. These screening costs are not itemized in the model. Fingerprinting mechanics and timelines were not verified.

**Required systems and costs the model includes.**

- **Billing, records and EVV.** Providers must hold a Medicaid ID to be paid [S14]. The model carries a per-resident software line as an operator estimate. NJ's EVV vendor is HHAeXchange, and DDD's EVV helpdesk is DDDEVV@dhs.nj.gov (email unverified) [S20].
- **Annual audit and Fiscal Sustainability Report.** The model includes a CPA audit line because modeled reimbursement exceeds $350,000 [S8]. The audit must follow GAAS. The Fiscal Sustainability Report is also due 120 days after the state fiscal year ends (about October 30) [S8].
- **Nurse consultant.** A nurse requirement was not verified in the 10:44A text reviewed. The model includes a registered nurse consultant as a prudent cost for residents with health needs.
- **Insurance.** No minimum liability, professional, abuse/molestation, auto or property insurance amounts were found. OPIA reviews insurance documents at administrative inspections [S1]. Premiums are operator estimates.
- **Housing and vehicle.** Housing must be cleared with DDD's housing office before acquisition [S1]. Vehicle costs are operator estimates.

**Compliance posture.** OPIA is increasing the frequency of unannounced inspections beginning in 2026 [S1]. Two consecutive provisional licenses may lead to non-renewal [S1]. Keep staff files, schedules and training certificates current at every residence at all times.
sections.market_conditions:
**Supply and competition.** About 2,300 licensed homes with capacity for over 9,600 individuals are reported, and nearly 80% of licensed provider agencies are non-profits [S16]. For-profit operators are a minority of agencies. Market shares, named competitors and the current count of DDD-approved residential providers were not found. A licensed agency list dated October 28, 2025 is published, and it does not represent that all of an agency's residential programs are licensed [S49].

**Wages.**

- DDD projects the NJ average DSP wage at about **$20.71 per hour** ($20.25 NCI 2024 average plus the about $0.46 per hour DSP and DSP Supervisor wage increase effective January 1, 2026); DDD also cites about $21 per hour for 2026 [S24]. The increase is funded by a $9.1M state allocation and must be passed through as a base-wage increase. The model uses $20.71 for DSPs.
- The statewide minimum wage is **$15.92 per hour** effective January 1, 2026 [S30]. A secondary source gives $16.48 on January 1, 2027 [S31]. A lower $15.23 rate for employers with fewer than six employees is secondary only [S32].
- A secondary source lists $18.92 per hour for direct care staff at long-term care facilities. Whether it applies to DD community residences is unconfirmed [S33]. The modeled $20.71 is above it.
- A secondary O*NET display of BLS May 2025 data puts the NJ home health and personal care aide median at $37,090 a year (about $17.83 per hour), with a 10th to 90th percentile of $32,220 to $48,180 [S37]. The national median for the occupation is $35,800 [S36].
- DDD's January 2026 update cites an NJ registered nurse mean of $51.44 per hour (May 2024 OEWS) [S24]. No NJ city sets its own minimum wage, per a secondary source [S33]. For metro context, the all-occupation mean hourly wage in the New York-Newark-Jersey City area was $41.50 in May 2025 [S38]. NJ BLS wages for supervisors, managers and billing staff were not verified, so those lines are operator estimates.

**Payroll costs.** The 2026 UI taxable wage base is $44,800, and the TDI/FLI wage base (workers only) is $171,100 [S30]. A secondary source puts the new-employer UI rate at 2.8% combined for the first three calendar years [S34]. FUTA and the employer TDI share are not modeled. The overall NJCRIB workers' compensation rate change effective January 1, 2026 is a 4.3% decrease [S35]. The class code and manual rate for residential care were not found.

**Housing.** HUD FY2026 fair market rents (40th percentile, residential proxies only) show how much the region matters for a four-bedroom home:

| Area | 3BR | 4BR |
|---|---|---|
| Newark HMFA (Essex/Union/Morris/Sussex) | $2,761 | $3,137 |
| Bergen-Passaic HMFA | $2,835 | $3,618 |
| Jersey City HMFA (Hudson) | $3,367 | $3,955 |

These come from the HUD table hosted by NJ Treasury [S39]. Actual group-home leases may run higher, and FY2027 FMRs were not verified.

**Funding trend.** DDD community program funding is growing (FY26 $3.81 billion, FY27 recommended $4.12 billion) [S46][S47]. The FY26 State Budget added about $164 million to DDD [S25]. Recent rate increases have been tied to DSP wages (1/1/2026) and training requirements (10/1/2024) [S23][S24].

**Entity costs.** Secondary sources give a $100 LLC Certificate of Formation fee (older sources say $125) and a $75 annual report fee. NJ does not impose an LLC franchise tax, per a secondary source. None of these was verified on the official Division of Revenue site [S40][S41][S42].
sections.financial_narrative:
**How the P&L is built.** Revenue per resident is *rate x units x share of residents*. Costs are DSP coverage hours at $20.71 per hour [S24], salaried supervisors, executive director, billing coordinator, an RN consultant, and a payroll burden of 23.5%. That burden is 10.5% payroll tax (employer FICA plus the 2.8% new-employer UI rate [S34]), 5% workers' compensation (operator estimate) and 8% benefits (operator estimate). Rent, utilities, vehicles, insurance, the annual audit, training and software are fixed or per-resident lines. Rent is fixed whether beds are full or not.

**The critical caveat.** The revenue per resident is an assumption. **No published 2026 DDD residential Individual Supports rate was found.** The model uses $12,500 per month ($150,000 a year) in most homes, $16,667 a month ($200,000 a year) for the higher-need home, and the Tier A allotment of $66,424 a year for the apartments. All are placed within or at the bottom of the secondary-source CCP allotment range of $66,424 to $527,838 [S27]. Allotments are caps, not payment guarantees. Resident room-and-board contributions are excluded because the rules were not verified.

**Results at the default occupancy (92%, an operator estimate).**

| Configuration | Net per month | Margin | Break-even occupancy | First profit month | Cash needed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Six 4-bed homes (24 residents, $150k) | $11,432 | 4.1% | 88.0% | 9 | $893,708 |
| One 6-bed home ($150k) | $8,694 | 12.6% | 79.8% | 5 | $131,148 |
| **Three 4-bed homes (12 residents, $150k) — default** | **$1,765** | **1.3%** | **90.8%** | **5** | **$315,640** |
| One 4-bed higher-need home (2 staff 24/7, $200k) | $880 | 1.4% | 90.6% | 4 | $126,072 |
| One 4-bed home ($150k) | -$1,933 | -4.2% | 96.1% | none | $175,991 |
| Two supervised apartments (8 residents, Tier A $66,424) | -$9,385 | -23.0% | 115.7% | none | $437,986 |

Four configurations are profitable at 92%, but two of them barely so. The single 4-bed home needs about 96% occupancy just to break even, which is at the optimistic bound. The apartment model cannot cover required costs at the lowest tier because break-even occupancy exceeds 100%. Do not assume DDD would authorize more than the tier allows.

**Why scale and bed count matter.** At the default 3-home configuration, modeled revenue at 92% occupancy is about $138,000 a month. Payroll (with burden) is about $109,000, roughly 79% of revenue by my arithmetic. The executive director, billing, audit, accounting and insurance costs are largely fixed. The 6-bed home does best because the same supervisor, director and audit are spread over six residents instead of four. That result depends on the assumption that a 6-bed home earns the same per-resident revenue and needs only about 1,350 DSP hours a month. No state staffing ratio was found, so verify against residents' ISPs and DDD authorizations. The 16-individual cap per residence leaves room to grow [S2], but siting and zoning were not researched.

**Sensitivities (arithmetic from the model).**

- **Rate:** At the default, a 1% change in revenue per resident is about $1,380 a month. The default breaks even at roughly $12,340 a month per resident (about $148,100 a year), only about 1.3% below the assumption. The 6-bed home breaks even near $10,900 a month (about $131,000 a year). A 5% rate shortfall on six homes costs about $13,800 a month and turns $11,432 into about -$2,370.
- **Occupancy:** In the default, each occupancy point is worth about $1,500 of revenue a month, so the conservative 88% case loses roughly $5,000 to $6,000 a month (linear approximation).
- **DSP wage:** Each $1.00 per hour increase on 3,000 DSP hours costs about $3,700 a month with burden. That is enough to turn the default from +$1,765 to about -$1,940. The same $1.00 costs about $7,400 on six homes (they remain positive at about $4,000) and about $1,670 on the 6-bed home. The statewide minimum rises to $16.48 in 2027 per a secondary source [S31]. The modeled $20.71 is already above the unconfirmed $18.92 long-term care rate [S33]. If a different DSP wage is needed to hire, recompute.
- **Rent:** Rent uses the Newark HMFA 4BR FMR of $3,137 per home [S39]. In the Jersey City area ($3,955) the cost rises by $818 per home. That is about $2,450 a month for three homes, which turns the default to about -$690. The same move on six homes still leaves them near $6,500. Bergen-Passaic ($3,618) adds about $480 per home.
- **Staffing intensity:** The higher-need home needs 2 staff 24/7 and a higher authorization. It earns only $880 a month at an assumed $200,000 a year per resident. Higher-need residents do not automatically mean higher profit.

**Timing and cash.** First-profit months are 4 to 9 depending on the configuration, and under FFS payment follows delivery [S12]. The cash needed figures include startup and the modeled ramp-up deficit. Larger agencies need far more cash. The six-home configuration needs about $894,000, and the workbook staffs all homes from month 1. Opening homes one at a time reduces the peak. Startup also includes an independent CPA examination (operator estimate $8,000 to $20,000) [S4].

**Path to profit, honestly.** Profit requires (1) confirming the real DDD authorized rate per resident, (2) admitting residents faster than DDD's limited waiting-list throughput may allow, (3) avoiding the single 4-bed model, and (4) keeping DSP and rent costs from rising. Do not raise assumed revenue or drop required costs to make a plan profit.
sections.risks:
**Rate risk (largest).** The 2026 DDD residential rate could not be read in the retrieved material, so revenue is assumed. A small percentage shortfall erases the default margin (about 1.3% at the default configuration). Allotments are caps, and actual authorizations may be lower [S27]. Rate changes can also add wage or training mandates without extra margin, as with the 1/1/2026 DSP and Supervisor wage pass-through that must be paid as base wages [S24] and the 10/1/2024 training-related rate change [S23].

**Eligibility and entry risk.** A 24-month service history is required before applying [S7]. The executive director qualifications are cumulative, and an owner who lacks any one must hire a qualifying director. The application can be denied if elements are missing after 45 days, with a six-month bar on reapplying [S4]. A prior denial elsewhere for substantial noncompliance bars issuance [S4].

**Referral and occupancy risk.** DDD reaches about 200 to 400 people a year from the Priority Waiting List [S44]. A person on the list is not guaranteed enrollment [S45]. Occupancy data is not available. If admissions run slower than one a month, each month adds fixed cost.

**Regulatory and enforcement risk.** Annual and unannounced inspections are increasing [S1]. Two consecutive provisional licenses may result in non-renewal [S1]. P.L.2025, c.280 strengthens DHS enforcement, and its content was not reviewed [S43]. N.J.A.C. 10:44A was readopted in 2026, and DHS says further rulemaking may be necessary [S6]. The 2023 rule text may not match current standards.

**Unverified requirements and unmodeled costs.** No staffing ratio, training hour totals, insurance minimums or licensing fees were found. Drug testing, registry checks, driver abstracts, fingerprinting, CPR and medication training, FUTA, employer TDI and the Fiscal Sustainability Report are not itemized in the model. Municipal zoning and Uniform Construction Code fire-safety specifics were not researched. Any of these could add cost or delay opening.

**Workforce risk.** DSP wages are the largest cost. A $1.00 per hour increase on three homes costs about $3,700 a month. The minimum wage rises to $16.48 in 2027 per a secondary source [S31]. The metro wage environment is high [S38].

**Cash and billing risk.** Providers bill after service delivery [S12]. Claims deny without a Medicaid ID [S14]. EVV compliance applies to Individual Supports codes [S18], and EVV exceptions delay payment. An audit is required above $350,000 in reimbursement [S8].

**Funding and budget risk.** FY27 increases (+$154M, rate increases, 318-person list removal) are proposals only [S26][S43][S47]. State policy could change.

**Housing risk.** Rent estimates use HUD FMR proxies [S39]. Real group-home leases may be higher. Rent is fixed even when beds are empty. Siting restrictions apply [S2].
sections.recommendations:
1. **Verify the rate first.** DDD has published FY26 rates (Quick Guide, effective 1/1/2026). Read the Individual Supports (H2016HI-series) tier rows, and email the DDD Provider Helpdesk (DDD.ProviderHelpdesk@dhs.nj.gov, email unverified [S7]) and DDD Fee-for-Service (DDD.FeeForService@dhs.nj.gov [S43]) to confirm procedure codes, billing units and your authorized tier. DDD's phone line is 800-832-9173. Replace the assumed $12,500 per resident per month in the workbook before committing capital.

2. **Confirm you meet the 24-month rule.** Document 24 months of direct care service history, with survey or audit results and plans of correction [S7]. If you do not have it, ask DDD how it can be demonstrated before you spend on housing.

3. **Avoid the single 4-bed and low-tier apartment models.** At the assumed rates they lose $1,933 and $9,385 a month. If you start small, a 6-bed home (up to the 16-person cap [S2]) fits the model better, subject to staffing, siting and zoning confirmation. A single 6-bed home earns about $8,694 a month at the assumed rate, with the lowest cash need of the profitable cases ($131,148). These figures predate pricing of the unmodeled compliance costs and should be rerun.

4. **Grow in steps.** The default three 4-bed homes show only a 1.3% margin and 90.8% break-even occupancy, so treat them as a transition stage. Six 4-bed homes reach about 4.1% margin but need about $894,000 of cash. Open homes one at a time and hire staff as each fills.

5. **Negotiate lease cost carefully.** Compare Newark, Bergen-Passaic and Jersey City rent levels [S39] before choosing a location, because a $818 per home increase wipes out the default margin. Consult DDD's Office of Housing and Resource Development before acquiring any property [S1].

6. **Protect staffing cost.** Test your staffing plan against each resident's ISP and DDD authorization, since no state ratio was found. Recompute at the actual DSP wage you need to hire, and pass the FY26 $0.46/hr increase through as a base-wage increase by 3/1/2026. The owner can fill the executive director role only if the owner meets all the cumulative 10:44A-2.5(a) requirements (bachelor's degree, five years of progressive DD management experience with two at a senior or supervisory level, and program and fiscal knowledge) [S2]. Otherwise budget for a qualifying hire.

7. **Prepare the application package early.** Engage a CPA for the two-year examination [S4]. Complete background checks for the agency head and owners [S4]. Draft the procedure manual and job descriptions [S4]. Respond to any missing items within 45 days [S4].

8. **Set up Medicaid and EVV before the first claim.** Complete the Combined Application and obtain the Medicaid ID [S13][S14]. Set up EVV with HHAeXchange and confirm with DDD how the live-in attestation applies [S19][S20].

9. **Price in compliance.** Budget for the annual audit (GAAS) and the Fiscal Sustainability Report due about October 30 [S8]. Also budget for insurance quotes, drug testing, registry and driver abstract checks, CPR and medication training, and inspection readiness for annual and unannounced visits [S1]. Keep staff files, schedules and training certificates current.

10. **Track the open items.** Watch whether the FY27 budget, rate increases and CCP waiting-list removals were enacted [S43][S47], any amendments to 10:44A [S6], and the content of P.L.2025, c.280 [S43].

checklist.task: Confirm your model needs an Office of Licensing license under N.J.A.C. 10:44A
checklist.instructions: The Office of Licensing says licensure is required when the setting is provider-managed. Group homes and supervised apartments that are provider-managed are covered. Read the OPIA licensing page and 10:44A-1.1 and decide which of your planned residences are provider-managed. No cost. Allow 1-2 days.

checklist.task: Rule out the owner-occupied alternative (N.J.A.C. 10:44B)
checklist.instructions: Community care residences, meaning Family Care or Skill Development in a private home or apartment, are licensed under 10:44B, not 10:44A. If you plan a shared home where the individual lives with the caregiver, you are on a different pathway. This bundle covers 10:44A provider-managed homes only.

checklist.task: Verify you have 24 months of prior direct care service history
checklist.instructions: Before the licensing application, DDD requires documented direct care service history of at least 24 months, including survey or audit results and plans of correction. If you do not have this history, you cannot start the pathway. Options are to build the history first, or to partner with or hire an established agency. Gather survey reports and plans of correction now. Time depends on your history.
checklist.cite: DDD Apply to Become a Provider

checklist.task: Check the prior-denial bar for every owner and applicant
checklist.instructions: No license is issued to a person previously denied a license by any State agency for substantial noncompliance or federal law violations. Review the history of all owners, officers and the executive director before spending money on the application.

checklist.task: Obtain the current text of N.J.A.C. 10:44A after the 2026 readoption
checklist.instructions: 10:44A was readopted effective February 17, 2026, with a new expiration of February 17, 2033. DHS stated further rulemaking may be necessary. The rule text available to this report is a Feb 2024 snapshot, so confirm with the Office of Licensing that nothing in the readopted text differs. Also check the NJ Register for any proposed amendments. No cost. Allow 1 day.

checklist.task: Understand the enforcement environment before you commit
checklist.instructions: The Office of Licensing is increasing unannounced inspections beginning in 2026. P.L.2025, c.280 (January 2026) enhances DHS enforcement authority over DD providers. The statute was not reviewed for this report, so read it with counsel, particularly the penalty provisions.

checklist.task: Understand how DD residential funding works before modeling
checklist.instructions: DDD runs two Medicaid waiver programs, the Supports Program and the Community Care Program (CCP), under NJ's Section 1115 demonstration. Residential-level Individual Supports are funded mainly through CCP. Providers bill Medicaid fee-for-service after delivering each service. Individuals must be 21+ and Medicaid-eligible. Your revenue depends on individuals who have CCP enrollment and choose your home.
checklist.cite: DDD Supports Program and Community Care; Transition Plan Addendum #3

checklist.task: Confirm the current 2026 Individual Supports residential rate and unit directly with DDD
checklist.instructions: No 2026 residential Individual Supports rate, procedure code or billing unit was found in any retrieved source. Rates for nine agency-provided services rose 1/1/2026. Email DDD.FeeForService@dhs.nj.gov for the current rate schedule and use only confirmed numbers in your pro forma. The Pro Forma uses an assumed authorized amount per resident, not a published rate.
checklist.cite: DDD FFS Rate Schedule; iRecord Rate Change 1/1/2026

checklist.task: Review demand context and referral realities
checklist.instructions: 3,665 people were on the CCP Priority Waiting List in FY26 (+511 vs FY25). DDD typically reaches 200-400 people a year from it. Being listed is not a guarantee of eligibility or enrollment, and DDD works through the list chronologically. A new provider has no guaranteed referral pipeline, so plan outreach to support coordination agencies and families.
checklist.cite: DDD Division Update 6/25/2026; DDD Waiting List page

checklist.task: Email the DDD Provider Helpdesk with your pathway questions
checklist.instructions: Contact DDD.ProviderHelpdesk@dhs.nj.gov with questions on licensed residential setting approval, the Combined Application, and Individual Supports. DDD designates this address for those questions. Keep every reply in your compliance file.
checklist.cite: DDD Apply to Become a Provider

checklist.task: Form your legal entity (typically a New Jersey LLC or nonprofit corporation)
checklist.instructions: File a Certificate of Formation with the NJ Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services. Secondary sources conflict on the fee ($100 vs $125), so confirm the current fee on the official site before filing. NJ imposes no LLC franchise tax per a secondary source. Nearly 80% of NJ licensed provider agencies are non-profits; weigh nonprofit status with counsel. Allow 1-2 weeks.
checklist.cite: N.J.S.A. Title 42 (LLC filing); fee not verified

checklist.task: Obtain proof of authorization to do business in New Jersey
checklist.instructions: The licensing application requires proof of New Jersey authorization to do business. Get your formation certificate and any state registration documents certified or copied as the application requires. Confirm the exact documents with the Office of Licensing.

checklist.task: Obtain a federal EIN
checklist.instructions: Apply free at irs.gov. It is issued immediately online. You need it for payroll, banking and the Medicaid application.

checklist.task: Calendar the NJ LLC annual report
checklist.instructions: A secondary source states the annual report fee is $75, due the last day of the formation anniversary month. The official fee was not verified. Add the date to your compliance calendar.
checklist.cite: NJ Division of Revenue annual report (fee not verified)

checklist.task: Decide the tax classification and note partnership filing fees if multi-owner
checklist.instructions: An LLC taxed as a partnership with more than two owners and NJ income may owe a $150 per-owner filing fee per one secondary source, which is unverified. Confirm with a CPA before choosing the structure.

checklist.task: Set up governance documents and name the executive director
checklist.instructions: The application requires organizational and governance detail for the applicant. Prepare an operating agreement or bylaws, ownership and officer list, and identify the executive director/agency head. The Office of Licensing lists this information in 10:44A-1.4, so match your documents to the current list.

checklist.task: Open a dedicated business bank account
checklist.instructions: Keep Medicaid receipts, payroll and any resident funds separate from personal funds. Bring the formation documents and EIN letter. Allow 1-3 days.

checklist.task: Retain a healthcare attorney with DDD licensing experience
checklist.instructions: Use the attorney for entity choice, lease review, the procedure manual and P.L.2025, c.280 exposure. The pro forma carries accounting, payroll and legal as an operator estimate of $600/month for one home.

checklist.task: Engage a CPA for the independent examination of finances required in the application
checklist.instructions: The application must include an independent examination of the organization's financial status, obtained from a CPA, for the two most recent fiscal years, with Management Letters. Engage the CPA early because this is a long-lead item. The pro forma carries $8,000-$20,000 as an operator estimate. Get a quote.

checklist.task: Plan for the annual financial statement audit
checklist.instructions: Provider agencies that claim $350,000 or more in combined CCP and Supports Program reimbursement must meet an annual financial statement audit requirement. Even a 4-bed home at modeled revenue exceeds this. The pro forma carries $15,000-$30,000 a year as an operator estimate depending on size. Confirm the current requirement with DDD.

checklist.task: Build the working capital reserve before opening
checklist.instructions: Under fee-for-service you bill after service delivery, so payroll and rent come first. The modeled cash needed ranges from about $126,000 (one higher-need 4-bed home) to about $894,000 (six homes). Treat these figures as a planning guide because revenue is assumed.

checklist.task: Stress-test the pro forma against your actual DDD authorizations
checklist.instructions: The default configuration uses an assumed $150,000 per resident per year, not a published rate. The single 4-bed home loses money at that level and the Tier A apartment model loses money. Replace assumptions with the amounts DDD authorizes before committing to leases.

checklist.task: Track the FY27 DDD budget and rate changes
checklist.instructions: The FY27 recommendation shows $4.12 billion in gross community funding and an additional $154.0 million in state funds for CCP and the Supports Program. Enactment of rate increases was not verified. Check the DDD webinar updates for final numbers.

checklist.task: Complete the Combined Application to Become a Medicaid/DDD Approved Provider
checklist.instructions: Licensure is initiated by completing and mailing the Combined Application, plus the Attestation for Individual Supports Provider. Applications go through the DDD Provider Portal per DDD's FAQ. Confirm the current submission method with the DDD helpdesk. No application fee was found in the sources reviewed.

checklist.task: Select Individual Supports as the service on the Combined Application
checklist.instructions: Agencies that want to operate a licensed residential setting must submit the Combined Application and select Individual Supports. Selecting the wrong service will delay you. Verify the selection with the DDD Provider Helpdesk.
checklist.cite: DDD Apply to Become a Provider

checklist.task: Understand that Medicaid approval is required before any claim
checklist.instructions: An agency must be a Medicaid-approved provider to submit claims for DDD services. NJ Medicaid denies claims from providers without Medicaid registration or a Medicaid ID. Do not admit residents expecting billing until your Medicaid ID is active.

checklist.task: Ask whether the federal Medicaid enrollment application fee applies to you
checklist.instructions: The CY2026 federal fee is $750 per a secondary source, which limits it to institutional providers, per service location, and not annual. Whether it applies to DDD residential providers was not verified. Ask DMAHS or the DDD helpdesk before budgeting. Plan $0-$750.

checklist.task: Collect the three professional references for the applicant and for the executive director
checklist.instructions: The application requires at least three professional references each, for the applicant and for the executive director. Request them early and confirm the reference format required.

checklist.task: Assemble the complete application package and track the 45-day completeness deadline
checklist.instructions: If all required elements are not received within 45 days of the initial submission, the application may be denied. A denied applicant cannot reapply for six months. Use a checklist of every element and submit all items together where possible.

checklist.task: Calendar the 60-day decision window
checklist.instructions: DHS must give written approval or non-approval within 60 calendar days of receipt of the completed application, extendable only in exceptional circumstances. Do not sign leases or hire staff in a way that cannot be unwound before approval. Timelines for steps after approval were not verified.

checklist.task: Confirm whether the combined license application amendment (PRN 2022-083) was adopted
checklist.instructions: The 10:44A-1.4 text points to the combined application. A 2022 proposal (PRN 2022-083) would add that language, and adoption was not independently verified. Ask the Office of Licensing which form and process is current.

checklist.task: Clear the criminal history check for the agency head before pay or contract
checklist.instructions: No agency head may be paid or contracted until the Department has determined that no criminal history record information exists on file. The check covers FBI and NJ State Police records. Fingerprinting mechanics were not verified, so ask the Office of Licensing for the current process. The pro forma carries $100-$600 as an operator estimate for checks.

checklist.task: Run the criminal history check for owners or the licensee if different from the agency head
checklist.instructions: If the agency head is not the owner or licensee, the owner(s) or licensee must also comply with a criminal history background check. Start these in parallel.

checklist.task: Confirm the executive director meets the 10:44A-2.5 qualifications
checklist.instructions: The rule lists a bachelor's degree and five years of progressive management experience working with people with developmental disabilities. The captured text did not show whether these are alternatives or cumulative. Ask the Office of Licensing and document the answer before naming your director.

checklist.task: Identify a qualified residence supervisor for each home
checklist.instructions: The supervisor responsible for operating a residence needs a high school diploma or equivalent and one year of experience working with people with developmental disabilities. The pro forma carries one supervisor per home at an operator estimate of $52,000 a year.

checklist.task: Set direct support professional hiring standards
checklist.instructions: DSPs must be at least 18 years old with a high school diploma or equivalent. Build these into job postings, applications and personnel files, because inspectors review staff files, credentials and background checks.

checklist.task: Check staff background check mechanics with the Office of Licensing
checklist.instructions: Fingerprinting, Central Registry and similar checks for staff were not verified in the sources reviewed. Ask the Office of Licensing which checks apply to each staff type and their timelines, and write the process into your procedure manual.

checklist.task: Consult DDD's Office of Housing and Resource Development before acquiring housing
checklist.instructions: OPIA advises: do not acquire housing before consulting with the Division's Office of Housing and Resource Development. No direct contact was verified, so go through the DDD helpdesk. Do this before signing any lease or purchase.

checklist.task: Check siting against the institutional proximity restriction
checklist.instructions: A residence may not be on the grounds of, or immediately adjacent to, public institutions serving a similar population. Verify the address against nearby facilities before you commit.

checklist.task: Size the residence within the capacity limits
checklist.instructions: A community residence under 10:44A may house up to 16 individuals. Supervised apartments may hold up to four individuals per apartment. The modeled homes are 4 and 6 beds, well under the cap.

checklist.task: Check municipal zoning and land-use rules for group homes
checklist.instructions: Local zoning treatment and any state-law protections for group homes were not researched. Ask a land-use attorney or the municipal zoning office before signing a lease. Allow 1-3 weeks.

checklist.task: Budget rent using local listings, not only HUD proxies
checklist.instructions: HUD FY2026 FMRs are residential proxies only. Newark HMFA 4BR is $3,137 and 3BR $2,761. Jersey City HMFA 4BR is $3,955. Bergen-Passaic 4BR is $3,618. Actual group-home leases may be higher. Rent is a fixed cost whether beds are filled or not.

checklist.task: Confirm building code and fire-safety requirements for the property
checklist.instructions: The Uniform Construction Code use-group and fire-safety specifics under 10:44A subchapter 6 could not be verified from a current text. Obtain the current subchapter, schedule a pre-inspection with the local code and fire officials, and budget for alarms, extinguishers and egress. The pro forma carries about $1,500 per home as an operator estimate.

checklist.task: Plan accessibility modifications for the residents you expect to serve
checklist.instructions: Match the home to the residents' needs, such as ramps, bathrooms and bedroom access. The pro forma carries about $5,000 per home as an operator estimate. Actual cost depends on the individuals.

checklist.task: Furnish and equip each home
checklist.instructions: Beds, appliances, housewares and common-area furniture. The pro forma carries about $6,000 per home as an operator estimate. Room and board rules for DDD residences, including how SSI of $994 per month applies, were not verified, so confirm what you may charge residents before planning to recover costs.

checklist.task: Write and submit the procedure manual to the Office of Licensing
checklist.instructions: Before opening, the applicant must submit a procedure manual to the Office of Licensing for approval. Draft it against the full text of 10:44A and have counsel review it. The pro forma carries $3,000-$10,000 as an operator estimate for the manual, policies and job descriptions.

checklist.task: Submit job descriptions to DDD after the procedure manual is approved
checklist.instructions: The applicant submits job descriptions to the Division of Developmental Disabilities for each table-of-organization position for review and approval. Build a table of organization first, covering executive director, supervisor, DSPs, nurse and billing roles.

checklist.task: Create the two-week staff schedule template and in-charge designation
checklist.instructions: Keep a written schedule covering at least two weeks at each residence, with full staff names. The employee in charge must be designated for each shift. Inspectors review schedules.

checklist.task: Write the emergency-availability procedure for times residents are away
checklist.instructions: Staff are not required on-site when no individuals are present, but trained staff familiar with the residents must be available for emergencies. Document who is on call and how they are reached.

checklist.task: Obtain the current awake-overnight and ratio rules from the Office of Licensing
checklist.instructions: No awake-overnight or per-shift ratio was found in the 10:44A text reviewed. The awake/asleep ratio found is in 10:44C (head injury) and does not apply. Ask the Office of Licensing what staffing is required and build your schedule to the answer and each resident's ISP.

checklist.task: Document incident management, abuse and neglect prevention procedures
checklist.instructions: Training on abuse and neglect prevention is part of basic DSP training, and enforcement authority was enhanced by P.L.2025, c.280. Align your incident reporting procedures with current DDD requirements. Confirm the current requirements with DDD.

checklist.task: Hire direct support staff at or above the wage floor
checklist.instructions: NJ minimum wage is $15.92 per hour from 1/1/2026. A secondary source lists $16.48 from 1/1/2027. A secondary source lists $18.92 for direct care staff at long-term care facilities, and whether this applies to DD residences is unconfirmed, so ask NJDOL. DDD projects the average NJ DSP wage at about $20.71 per hour after the 1/1/2026 increase, which the pro forma uses. The NJ median for home health aides is $37,090 a year.

checklist.task: Complete basic DDD-required training for every DSP within 90 days of hire
checklist.instructions: Each DSP must complete basic staff training required by the Division within 90 days of employment. Topics include DDD Shifting Expectations, abuse and neglect prevention, and first aid. Required hour totals were not verified. Track completion dates in each file.

checklist.task: Obtain first aid certification from an ECC-compliant provider
checklist.instructions: First aid training must come from a training entity that meets current Emergency Cardiovascular Care (ECC) guidelines, with a valid certificate on file. A per-shift first aid and CPR rule was seen only in a 2005 version and is unconfirmed, so ask the Office of Licensing about shift coverage.

checklist.task: Hire a registered nurse consultant
checklist.instructions: A nurse requirement was not verified in the 10:44A text reviewed, but residents with health needs and medications make nursing oversight prudent. The pro forma carries $50 per hour and 2 hours per resident per month as an operator estimate. NJ RN wages were not verified.

checklist.task: Plan for NJ wage-floor increases and local labor competition
checklist.instructions: A secondary source reports no NJ city sets its own minimum wage. The BLS all-occupation mean wage in the NY-Newark-Jersey City area is $41.50 per hour, which signals a tight labor market. Budget annual wage increases and test the pro forma with higher DSP wages.

checklist.task: Set up personnel files that match the inspection checklist
checklist.instructions: Office of Licensing inspections review staff files, schedules, credentials and background checks. Keep for each employee the application, ID and education proof, background check clearance, training certificates and first aid certificate.

checklist.task: Set up Electronic Visit Verification with HHAeXchange
checklist.instructions: NJ's contracted EVV vendor is HHAeXchange. DDD Individual Supports codes (for example H2016HI, H2016HI22, H2016HIU88) are on NJ's EVV list. Use the DDD EVV helpdesk at DDDEVV@dhs.nj.gov for onboarding. The vendor cost to providers was not verified.

checklist.task: Learn the live-in worker EVV exemption and attestation
checklist.instructions: CMS allows EVV exclusion when the person providing care lives with the person receiving care. A Live-In Worker Attestation is required. Apply only where it truly fits your staffing model.

checklist.task: Check current EVV compliance deadlines
checklist.instructions: NJ went live with EVV for DDD Individual Supports, In-Home Respite and Community-Based Supports on 1/1/2021. Current 2026-2027 compliance deadlines were not verified. Ask DDDEVV@dhs.nj.gov.

checklist.task: Set up a billing process for fee-for-service claims
checklist.instructions: Providers bill Medicaid for specific services after delivering them rather than receiving monthly contract allotments. Confirm procedure codes, units and authorization requirements with DDD.FeeForService@dhs.nj.gov. Reconcile claims to authorizations monthly.

checklist.task: Choose records, scheduling and billing software
checklist.instructions: The pro forma carries about $75 per resident per month as an operator estimate. Get vendor quotes and confirm the software works with HHAeXchange and DDD portal requirements.

checklist.task: Obtain liability, professional, abuse/molestation, auto and property insurance
checklist.instructions: No numeric minimum insurance amounts were found for DD community residences or DDD provider approval. Inspectors review insurance documents at central office administrative reviews. Get quotes from carriers experienced in DD residential programs. The pro forma carries $700 per month for one home as an operator estimate.

checklist.task: Place workers' compensation coverage
checklist.instructions: Get quotes through an NJ broker. The NJCRIB approved a 4.3% overall rate decrease effective 1/1/2026. The class code and manual rate for residential care were not found. The pro forma uses 5% of payroll as an operator estimate.

checklist.task: Register for NJ employer payroll taxes
checklist.instructions: The 2026 UI taxable wage base is $44,800 and the TDI/FLI wage base is $171,100. A secondary source says new employers pay a flat 2.8% combined UI rate for the first three years, and the official rate table was not found. Confirm your rate with NJDOL. A full-time DSP at $20.71 per hour earns about $43,077, which is under the UI base.

checklist.task: Use a payroll provider and set a compliant pay schedule
checklist.instructions: Configure NJ UI, TDI/FLI and withholding. Budget the payroll service within the accounting, payroll and legal line.

checklist.task: Do not own or operate a residence without Office of Licensing authorization
checklist.instructions: No person may own or operate a community residence for individuals with developmental disabilities without authorization from the Office of Licensing. Do not admit residents until you hold written authorization. Confirm issuance steps with the Office of Licensing because the timeline beyond the 60-day decision window was not verified.

checklist.task: Prepare for the on-site inspection
checklist.instructions: Each residence is subject to an annual on-site inspection by the Office of Licensing, and DHS may inspect without limitation or notice. Run an internal mock inspection covering staff files, schedules, credentials and background checks, the physical plant, and insurance documents.

checklist.task: Understand license types and the term
checklist.instructions: A full license is effective for up to one year. Partial compliance can lead to a provisional license, and two consecutive provisional licenses may result in non-renewal. Plan to reach substantial compliance on the first inspection.
checklist.cite: N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3; OPIA Office of Licensing page

checklist.task: Ask the Office of Licensing for current fees and renewal timelines
checklist.instructions: No license, application, renewal or inspection fee provision was found in the 10:44A-1.4 text reviewed, and renewal timelines were not verified. Ask in writing and add any fees to your budget. The pro forma carries no licensing fee.

checklist.task: Plan admissions through support coordinators and DDD
checklist.instructions: Individuals must be 21+ and Medicaid-eligible, and individuals choose a provider. Introduce your agency to support coordination agencies and families. The pro forma assumes about one admission a month, which is an operator estimate. Pace is not under your control.

checklist.task: Verify the Office of Licensing contact details
checklist.instructions: The only phone and PO Box found were on a 2005 rule version and are unconfirmed. Use the OPIA Contact Us form on the licensing page and keep a record. Do not rely on outdated contact details.

checklist.task: Keep the two-week written schedule current at every residence
checklist.instructions: The schedule must show full staff names and the in-charge employee for each shift. Post or file it per the procedure manual. Check it weekly.

checklist.task: Run a training tracker for 90-day DDD training, first aid and refreshers
checklist.instructions: Track each DSP's hire date, 90-day deadline and certificates. Late training is an easy inspection finding. Review monthly.

checklist.task: Prepare for unannounced inspections
checklist.instructions: The Office of Licensing is increasing unannounced inspections beginning in 2026. Keep files, schedules and records inspection-ready at all times. Assign one person per home to host inspectors.

checklist.task: Respond promptly to citations with plans of correction
checklist.instructions: Survey and audit results and plans of correction become part of your service history. Respond in writing by the deadline in each notice. Avoid back-to-back provisional licenses.

checklist.task: Monitor DDD updates and rate changes
checklist.instructions: DDD publishes division update webinars and rate notices, such as the 1/1/2026 increase for nine services to fund DSP training requirements. Review each update and adjust your budget. Self-directed billable rates were not increased.

checklist.task: Monitor 10:44A amendments
checklist.instructions: DHS said further rulemaking may be necessary after the 2026 readoption. Watch the NJ Register and DHS notices.

checklist.task: File the annual LLC report and renew insurance on schedule
checklist.instructions: Add the LLC report date, insurance renewals and workers' compensation audit dates to a compliance calendar.

checklist.task: Review the profitability of each home monthly
checklist.instructions: In the modeled results, one 6-bed home and six 4-bed homes were profitable at the default occupancy, while a single 4-bed home and the Tier A supervised apartments were not. Margins depend on assumed revenue. Reconcile against actual claims and adjust staffing to residents' authorizations.

checklist.task: Watch the audit threshold as you grow
checklist.instructions: Agencies claiming $350,000 or more in combined CCP and Supports Program reimbursement need an annual financial statement audit. Plan the engagement before year-end and keep records audit-ready.

checklist.task: Add homes only after the first home is stable
checklist.instructions: Add a home when occupancy, billing and inspections are steady. The pro forma staffs every home from month 1, so open one at a time. This reduces the cash needed.

checklist.task: Track the CCP waiting list and the state budget for demand signals
checklist.instructions: The CCP Priority Waiting List grew to 3,665 in FY26. The FY27 proposal funds removal of 318 people, and enactment was not verified. More removals mean more residential placements.
